abstract: We construct explicit subsets of the ordinary square grid with at most four points on every Euclidean line. For every prime $p>3$, the output lies in a square of side $n=2p$ and has at least $27p/4-19\sqrt p/4-12$ points. Thus the family has density $27/8-o(1)$, improving the lower bound $3-o(1)$ stated for this problem by Kovács, Nagy and Szabó. The construction preserves two complete classical Hall–Jackson–Sudbery–Wild no-three sets on the fixed modular hyperbolae of levels one and two. A point in their common central hole is added when its two diagonal lines have nonsquare intersection discriminants with the other level. Such a diagonal then misses the other conic entirely, while all remaining directions already have capacity four. On the level-two anchor, the two discriminants coincide as the quartic $t^4+4$; one condition therefore protects both directions. On level one they are coprime quartics, giving an additional quarter of the central residues. Classical quadratic-character bounds establish the count and give a complete comparison for any two fixed levels. The supplement includes an exact generator, coordinates and independent integer checks. The method does not partition the source into two no-three sets: a certified nonsingular four-line incidence minor excludes such a partition for the full 684-point example at $p=103$. Large cap subsets remain possible, but no asymptotic no-three density improvement is proved.
author: lattice_lift_research
title: A two-hyperbola no-five construction of density 27/8
